report_findings.title: Recognition must attach to a specific proposition
report_findings.text: The strongest standing disagreement concerns the conditional advice against removal warnings when no current removal plan exists. The retained 33453 proposal body attributes, quotes, and applies that expectation. This supports the inherited local-recognition judgment even though two fresh coders selected text_only. Local support does not require a binding project-wide rule. Exact assent to a definition of deprecation remains more interpretive: it can recognize an institutional status or simply endorse terminology. The explicit nonblocking-nits reply provides a clearer shared example of local recognition. Sources: 32714-body, 33453-body, 32406-180, and 32406-151.

report_findings.title: Documentary support depends on scope and date
report_findings.text: General guidance on moderation documents a procedure for warnings and bans; it does not independently verify the particular future sanction announced to a named contributor. Similarly, a later contribution guide supports discretionary merit weighting without proving the exact wording or force of an earlier categorical reminder. Broad maintainer release responsibility and deference on one backport decision are related but distinct evidence claims. Several standing differences arise because coders classify these different levels of specificity under one label. Sources: 32359-115, 32406-169, 32406-252, 33453-018, D_CONTRIB, and D_MOD.

report_findings.title: Matching labels can conceal provenance errors
report_findings.text: Within the body of PR 32381, a separate recommendation advocates proceeding with PR 32359. Two coders attach closure metadata for the containing PR to that recommendation. Both PRs closed unmerged, so the status labels match while the evidence targets differ. The correction is to attach the referenced proposal’s metadata or retain the containing proposal’s closure only as episode context. The audit also identified pronouns anchored to the wrong predicate occurrence and incomplete evidence arrays. Exact text matching alone did not detect those semantic targeting problems. Findings SA09, SA14, SA16, SA20, and SA21 preserve the repairs.

report_findings.title: Higher level claims require bounded alternatives
report_findings.text: The statement that a majority decides the winner supplies no electorate, threshold, jurisdiction, or decision procedure. Unknown is the least assumptive target level; constitutional and epistemic readings remain alternatives. The transparency statement more clearly expresses a contested legitimacy expectation, but its target can concern either the foundations of legitimate decisions or recurring decision procedures. The observed exchange does not establish adoption of a new arrangement. A thematic contrast between majority and merit claims also does not prove that they contest the same decision object. Sources: 32359-227, 32359-115, 32406-228, and 32406-229.

report_findings.title: The absolute freeze claim faces a counterproposal
report_findings.text: All three coders identify a categorical prohibition on translation-source updates after the final freeze and flag a dispute in its application. The proposed workaround would permit a source change while limiting translation disruption. It recognizes the reason for a freeze without independently establishing the absolute rule, a formal exception, or actual final translation processing. The inherited U32 annotation should therefore retain its limited evidentiary status while explicitly acknowledging this application challenge. Sources: 33224-010, 33224-015, 33224-019, and D_TRANSLATION.

report_findings.title: Extraction differences need meaning and scope checks
report_findings.text: Some inventory differences preserve meaning through different layers or subdivisions, including a user’s mempool-control claim and the distinction between possible future deprecation and a preferred removal schedule. The two unresolved alignment groups concern where a quoted premise and a tentative 150-byte refinement are stored. The full annotations retain those details in context or evidence, but the focal units do not attach them consistently. These are not established wholesale omissions. A shared convention deviation also survives: all three label a repeated literal bot question with a nonquestion speech act. Findings SA05, SA11, SA12, SA18, SA22, and SA23 retain these distinctions.

report_findings.title: The central evidentiary boundaries survive
report_findings.text: All three distinguish the reported addition of a source comment from verification of its exact wording, an announced moderation consequence from an observed ban, and repository integration from Bitcoin network adoption. They reproduce the supplied sequence of deprecation and warning edits while avoiding a permanent maintenance commitment or a fixed removal timetable. These agreements support the bounded reconstruction. The retained proposal bodies also show explicit attribution across proposals, but absent version histories the analysis cannot date the insertion of every quoted sentence or establish its causal effect on merger.
